_comment: Expected publication outcome per basket name for the pre-deploy gate (scripts/valuation_canary_summary.py --expect). Change an entry only together with the engine change that explains it, and say why here. 2026-09-27: calibrated premium (3.24%) is the default. 2026-10-02: a sound model that well-covered analysts do not back is published with a confidence alert (FLAGGED) instead of withheld; WITHHELD now means the model itself supports no single value (a failed or contradicting method, stale statements, a method the company does not fit) and the answer is the range.

NVDA.why: Calibrated premium lifts the DCF to about +57%; the 59-analyst Street target (+46%) covers more than half the move in the same direction.

MSFT.why: DCF about +14% with the calibrated premium; the Street (+12%) corroborates if it lands above 15%.

META.why: Calibrated premium lifts the DCF to about +23%; the Street target (+5%) covers less than half the move. Published with a confidence alert since 2026-10-02 (was withheld).

GOOGL.why: DCF about +15% with the calibrated premium; the Street (+25%) corroborates if it lands above 15%.

CRH.why: DCF about +25% with the calibrated premium; the Street (+57%) corroborates.

TSLA.why: Consensus cash flows support a value far below the market while the Street target sits above it; the exit leg is unavailable above the 80x boundary, which omits it rather than failing it. Published with a confidence alert since 2026-10-02 (was withheld).

AMD.why: DCF far below market on a 30%-capped fade; the Street target sits at the market, so nothing corroborates the gap. Published with a confidence alert since 2026-10-02 (was withheld).

AAPL.why: DCF-only, about -38% vs market; Street at the market. Published with a confidence alert since 2026-10-02 (was withheld).

AMZN.why: DCF about -29% vs market while the Street is +31%: model and Street point opposite ways, so it publishes with a confidence alert whenever its statements are current. Range only while they are not. On 2026-10-02 the provider had Amazon's June-2026 income statement but no balance sheet or cash flow for that quarter, so the last complete quarter (2026-03-31) was past the 150-day limit and the annual filing (2025-12-31) past the 200-day limit. The engine before 2026-10-02 carried the same statements blocker behind its Street reason, where a reader of the first sentence never saw it; the first pre-deploy gate run found it.

PYPL.why: DCF well above market while the Street target sits at the market. Published with a confidence alert since 2026-10-02 (was withheld).

MC.PA.why: Latest annual filing beyond the 200-day limit and no semiannual bridge. Range only: stale statements are a model input problem, not a disagreement with the Street.

PCJEWELLER.NS.why: Perpetual DCF is negative; a failed leg never publishes. Range only.

MU.why: Memory maker valued mid-cycle: the Street's two covered years, then revenue back to trend and a 21% DRAM through-cycle operating margin. Far below the price while the Street sits above it, so published with a confidence alert.

GM.why: GM Financial is a consolidated captive lender; scenario only until an operating/finance split exists. Range only.

TEX.why: Acquisition debt but no lending arm keeps its DCF. BORDERLINE: DCF about +74% needs the Street (+39%) to cover half the move (37%).

BKNG.why: Reports no cost of revenue in any year (expenses by function). It must build and pass integrity: before 2026-09-27 every Booking model failed the historical-period check, and payables measured against the absent line were projected at zero. Any publication outcome is accepted because the methods span right at the 1.8x limit: DCF about +34%, comps about +134% on Airbnb, Hilton and Royal Caribbean at 26.7x EBITDA versus Booking's own 12.2x. When the methods land inside the limit the value publishes, flagged if the Street does not back it.

SNDK.why: NAND-only memory maker valued mid-cycle: the Street's two covered years, then revenue back to trend and an 18% NAND through-cycle operating margin. Far below the price while the Street sits above it, so published with a confidence alert.
